rounds.text: Mehai Technology Ltd trades at a steep discount with a price-to-book ratio of 0.35x against a book value of ₹ 2.92, while sitting at a P/E of 10.6 that falls below the sector benchmark of 17.71x [E1, E2, E6, E7]. A discounted cash flow model suggests a valuation of ₹ 4 per share, leaving a substantial 74.0% margin of safety compared to the current market price of ₹ 1.02, with a reverse DCF showing the price merely assumes -0.7% growth against a base expectation of 18.0% [E37, E38, E39]. Fundamental performance displays robust multi-year expansion, highlighted by 142% compounded sales growth and 148% compounded profit growth over three years, alongside recent positive quarterly results showing net profit up 14% year-over-year [E14, E16, E53, E57]. Furthermore, the company generated ₹ 14 Cr in operating cash flow for March 2026 with a strong cash conversion of 1.75x, and promoter holdings recently rebounded with a 4.91% increase over the last quarter [E28, E29, E44]. Conceded: ROCE sits at a modest 5.51% to 7.4% and the trailing twelve months show a compounded sales decline of -6% alongside rising debtor and working capital days [E10, E12, E15, E47, E49].

The bear case against Mehai Technology Ltd centres on severe fundamental deterioration, alarming capital allocation strains, and persistent downward price momentum. Compounded sales and profit growth have turned negative over the trailing twelve months at -6% and -4% respectively [E15, E17], while operating margins have compressed by 2 percentage points over three years alongside an inconsistent trajectory [E24, E26]. Return profiles remain depressed, evidenced by a 3-year median ROE of just 6% and a recent ROCE of 5.51%, both trailing sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E22]. Operational efficiency is rapidly unwinding as debtor days stretch from 93 to 112 days and working capital requirements more than double from 110 days to 234 days [E47, E49]. This working capital drain has caused free cash flow to plummet to Rs -18 Cr alongside a sharp surge in borrowings from Rs 39 Cr to Rs 64 Cr [E30, E33], while insiders continue to exit with promoter holding dropping by 10.8 percentage points since December 2023 [E35]. Conceded: [E37].

Conceded: [E15, E17, E24, E26, E47, E49, E33]. While trailing numbers show compression [E15, E17, E24], the 3-year track record proves a powerful expansion with compounded sales growth at 142% and profit growth at 148% [E14, E16]. The bear highlights compressed return profiles [E9, E10], but ignores that the current P/E of 10.2x trades at a steep discount to the sector benchmark of 17.71x [E6], and the P/B of 0.34x heavily undercuts the sector benchmark of 1.38x [E7]. Conceded: [E30, E35]. However, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price of ₹ 1.02 already assumes a pessimistic -0.7% earnings growth against an 18.0% base case [E39], meaning immense pessimism is fully priced in while insider sentiment has recently reversed with promoter holding increasing by 4.91% over the last quarter [E44].

Conceded: [E14, E16]. Although the bull cites 3-year growth metrics, trailing data reveals severe deceleration with compounded sales growth at -6% and profit growth at -4% [E15, E17]. Conceded: [E39]. However, the bull's reliance on deep value discounts is countered by exploding working capital requirements, where debtor days have lengthened to 112 days [E47] and working capital days have ballooned from 110 to 234 days [E49], driving free cash flow down to a staggering negative ₹ 18 Cr [E30]. Furthermore, despite the bull's focus on recent quarterly insider accumulation [E44], long-term promoter commitment has deteriorated significantly, with promoter holdings dropping by 10.8% over the last three years [E48].
